        "contents": "This feature appears to be well-developed with a sophisticated implementation using XyFlow (ReactFlow). It includes custom nodes, connections between different entity types, and interactive features.\n\n## 3. Database Integration\n\nThe application uses Xata as its database, which appears to be a PostgreSQL-based database with added functionality.\n\n**Schema:**\nThe database schema includes tables for:\n\n- sightings\n- personnel (experts/key figures)\n- events\n- topics\n- organizations\n- testimonies\n- documents\n- artifacts\n- locations\n- user data (saved items, theories)\n\n**Implementation:**\nThe database integration appears complete with model definitions, server actions for data fetching, and utility functions for data transformation.\n\n## Next Steps for Implementation\n\nBased on the roadmap and existing code, here are the recommended next steps:\n\n1. **Complete the Sightings Globe Visualization**:\n   - Implement or refine the time slider for navigating sightings over time\n   - Add clustering functionality for better performance with large datasets\n   - Enhance the HUD interface with detailed information on selected sightings\n   - Display sightings data dispersed across the map grouped by decade rather than individual years\n   - Implement visualization controls to toggle between decade view and other time period views\n\n2. **Enhance the Mind Map Feature**:\n   - Add search functionality for finding entities in the graph\n   - Implement filtering by entity type\n   - Add user annotations and notes to graph entities\n\n3. **Topic Tracker Implementation**:\n   - Build on the existing mind map to create a dedicated topic tracking feature\n   - Implement trending topics visualization\n   - Add user engagement features for discussion\n\n4. **Library of Documents and Evidence**:\n   - Create a browsable interface for the documents in the database\n   - Implement search and filtering\n   - Add document previews and detailed metadata display\n\n",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "\n## Feature Roadmap\n\n### **1. Major Historical UFO Event Chronology**\n\n**a. Beautiful 3D Visuals of All UFO Sightings by Location**\n\n- **Interactive World Map**: Implement a dynamic, zoomable 3D globe where users can explore UFO sightings globally.\n- **Time Slider**: Allow users to navigate through time to see how sightings have evolved over decades.\n- **Heatmaps**: Display density of sightings in specific regions or time periods.\n- **Augmented Reality (AR) Integration**: Enable users to visualize historical sightings in their current location using AR.\n\n**b. Detailed Event Pages**\n\n- **Comprehensive Descriptions**: Provide in-depth information about each event, including eyewitness accounts, official reports, and media coverage.\n- **Multimedia Integration**: Incorporate photos, videos, audio recordings, and interactive media related to each event.\n- **Geospatial Data**: Show precise locations with satellite imagery and maps.\n- **User Annotations**: Allow users to add comments or additional information to each event.\n\n### **2. Status Reporting on Claims, Hearings, News Items, and Events**\n\n**a. Progress Reporting**\n\n- **Dashboard Overview**: Present a real-time dashboard highlighting recent developments, ongoing investigations, and upcoming events.\n- **Timeline Tracking**: Visual timelines showing the progression of key claims and hearings.\n- **Notification System**: Enable users to subscribe to updates on specific topics or events.\n\n**b. Categorization and Filtering**\n\n- **Filter by Date, Region, or Topic**: Allow users to sort and view status reports based on their interests.\n- **Priority Indicators**: Highlight high-impact or high-interest items for quick access.\n\n### **3. Topic Tracker**\n\n**a. Dynamic Topic Mapping**\n\n- **Interconnected Topics**: Visualize how different topics relate to each other using network graphs.\n- **Trending Topics**: Highlight emerging topics and their growth over time.\n",

        "contents": "### A. General Migration Strategy\n\n* **Primary Keys:** Xata uses string/char-based unique IDs like &#96;rec_abc123...&#96;. Maintain these as &#96;id&#96; (type: &#96;text&#96; or &#96;varchar&#96;) in Supabase to preserve all foreign key integrity and relationships.\n* **Foreign Keys:** Ensure that any &#96;link&#96; or relation columns point to the Xata-format char IDs, not integer autoincrements.\n* **Data Types:** Closest Postgres types are suggested below. Pay particular attention to:\n  * &#96;vector&#96;: Use &#96;vector&#96; extension or &#96;float[]&#96;.\n  * &#96;file&#96;, &#96;file[]&#96;: Use &#96;text[]&#96; or a Supabase Storage integration pattern.\n  * &#96;text&#96;, &#96;string&#96;: Use &#96;text&#96; or &#96;varchar&#96;.\n  * &#96;multiple&#96;: Use &#96;text[]&#96; or a dedicated join table if needed.\n  * &#96;json&#96;: Use &#96;jsonb&#96;.\n* **Empty Tables:** Some tables have no columns; just duplicate structure for now.\n* **Uniqueness:** Check/port all unique constraints, especially on &#96;title&#96;, &#96;email&#96;, etc.\n\n---\n\n### B. Tables to Create (Xata parity in Supabase)\n\n#### 1. topics\n\n* id (&#96;text&#96; primary key)\n* name (&#96;text&#96;)\n* summary (&#96;text&#96;)\n* photo (&#96;text&#96;) or (&#96;text[]&#96; if you want to future-proof)\n* photos (&#96;text[]&#96;)\n* title (&#96;text&#96;, unique)\n* embedding (&#96;vector(1536)&#96; or &#96;float[]&#96;)\n* ⮩ links: [topic-subject-matter-experts], [topics-testimonies], [event-topic-subject-matter-experts], [user-saved-topics]\n\n#### 2. personnel\n\n* id (&#96;text&#96; primary key)\n* bio (&#96;text&#96;)\n* role (&#96;text&#96;)\n* photo (&#96;text[]&#96;)\n* rank, credibility, popularity, authority (&#96;integer&#96;)\n* name (&#96;text&#96;, unique)\n* embedding (&#96;vector(1536)&#96; or &#96;float[]&#96;)\n* ⮩ links: [organization-members], [event-subject-matter-experts], etc.\n\n#### 3. events\n\n* id, name, description, location, latitude, longitude, date, photos, metadata, title (unique), summary, category (&#96;text[]&#96;), embedding (&#96;vector&#96;)\n* ⮩ links: [event-subject-matter-experts], etc.\n\n#### 4. organizations\n\n* id, name, specialization, description, photo, image, title(unique), embedding (vector 500)\n* ⮩ links: [organization-members], etc.\n\n#### 5. sightings\n\n",

        "originalContents": "\n\n/**\n * Test the Xata connection\n * @returns Connection status object\n */\nexport async function testConnection(): Promise\u003c{\n\tconnected: boolean;\n\ttables: string[];\n\tmessage: string;\n}\u003e {\n\ttry {\n\t\tconst client = getXataClient();\n\t\t// In a real implementation, we would make a simple query to test the connection\n\t\t// and list available tables\n\n\t\t// Mock success response\n\t\treturn {\n\t\t\tconnected: true,\n\t\t\ttables: [\n\t\t\t\t\"testimonies\",\n\t\t\t\t\"events\",\n\t\t\t\t\"personnel\",\n\t\t\t\t\"organizations\",\n\t\t\t\t\"artifacts\",\n\t\t\t],\n\t\t\tmessage: \"Successfully connected to Xata database\",\n\t\t};\n\t} catch (error) {\n\t\treturn {\n\t\t\tconnected: false,\n\t\t\ttables: [],\n\t\t\tmessage: &#96;Connection failed: ${(error as Error).message}&#96;,\n\t\t};\n\t}\n}",

        "contents": "2. **Relations:** Ensure any join/linking tables reference the correct IDs.\n3. **Migrate Data**: Import CSVs, preserving all original IDs (never auto-generate!).\n4. **Test Foreign Key Integrity:** After import, check every foreign key constraint resolves.\n5. **Validate Uniqueness Constraints:** Use SQL to find duplicates on fields that should be unique (esp. emails, titles, etc).\n6. **Handle Files/Media:** If mapping to Supabase Storage, create URLs or bucket pointers.\n7. **Vectors:** If using pgvector, enable extension; if not, store as float[].\n\n---\n\n### D. Notes\n\n* **DO NOT use Postgres serial/integer PKs** unless you're 100% sure you can remap all FKs in all joined/linking tables. To avoid breakage, just mirror Xata's &#96;id&#96; as text/varchar.\n* **Custom types**: For any &#96;multiple&#96; or enum types, consider mapping to a suitable text[] or dedicated join table.\n* **Tables with no columns** can be created as just a PK stub. Add columns as needed if schema evolves.\n",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "# Database Provider Registry Documentation\n\n## Overview\n\nThe &#96;registry.ts&#96; file creates a provider registry for database connections in the application. This implementation follows a centralized registry pattern which provides a clean abstraction layer for accessing different database providers.\n\n## Key Components\n\n1. **PROVIDERS Object**:\n   - A centralized registry that currently only includes Xata as a data provider\n   - Designed to be extendable with additional providers (Supabase, Convex, etc.)\n   - Exported as a constant with readonly typing\n\n2. **Type Definitions**:\n   - &#96;ProviderRegistry&#96;: Type representing the shape of the PROVIDERS object\n   - &#96;ProviderKey&#96;: Type representing the valid keys for accessing providers (currently just \"xata\")\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Centralized Access\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { PROVIDERS } from \"@/packages/db/registry\";\n\n// Access any provider\nconst data = await PROVIDERS.xata.db.events.getAll();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Provider Selection\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { PROVIDERS, type ProviderKey } from \"@/packages/db/registry\";\n\nfunction getDataWithProvider(providerKey: ProviderKey) {\n  const provider = PROVIDERS[providerKey];\n  return provider.db.someTable.getAll();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Implementation Details\n\nThe registry is implemented as a simple object that imports and aggregates initialized database clients:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { xata } from \"./xata/client\";\n\nexport const PROVIDERS = {\n  xata,\n  // Future additions:\n  // supabase: supabaseClient,\n  // convex: convexClient,\n} as const;\n\nexport type ProviderRegistry = typeof PROVIDERS;\nexport type ProviderKey = keyof ProviderRegistry;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Benefits\n\n1. **Abstraction**: Provides a clean interface for database access\n2. **Extensibility**: Makes it easy to add new providers\n3. **Consistency**: Ensures consistent access to different data sources\n4. **Discoverability**: Makes available providers easy to discover and use\n\n## Monorepo Architecture Integration\n\n",
        "detailedLines": [
          {

        "originalContents": "# Database Provider Registry Documentation\n\n## Overview\n\nThe &#96;registry.ts&#96; file creates a provider registry for database connections in the application. This implementation follows a centralized registry pattern which provides a clean abstraction layer for accessing different database providers.\n\n## Key Components\n\n1. **PROVIDERS Object**:\n   - A centralized registry that currently only includes Xata as a data provider\n   - Designed to be extendable with additional providers (Supabase, Convex, etc.)\n   - Exported as a constant with readonly typing\n\n2. **Type Definitions**:\n   - &#96;ProviderRegistry&#96;: Type representing the shape of the PROVIDERS object\n   - &#96;ProviderKey&#96;: Type representing the valid keys for accessing providers (currently just \"xata\")\n\n## Usage Examples\n\n### Centralized Access\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { PROVIDERS } from \"@/packages/db/registry\";\n\n// Access any provider\nconst data = await PROVIDERS.xata.db.events.getAll();\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Provider Selection\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { PROVIDERS, type ProviderKey } from \"@/packages/db/registry\";\n\nfunction getDataWithProvider(providerKey: ProviderKey) {\n  const provider = PROVIDERS[providerKey];\n  return provider.db.someTable.getAll();\n}\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Implementation Details\n\nThe registry is implemented as a simple object that imports and aggregates initialized database clients:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;typescript\nimport { xata } from \"./xata/client\";\n\nexport const PROVIDERS = {\n  xata,\n  // Future additions:\n  // supabase: supabaseClient,\n  // convex: convexClient,\n} as const;\n\nexport type ProviderRegistry = typeof PROVIDERS;\nexport type ProviderKey = keyof ProviderRegistry;\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Benefits\n\n1. **Abstraction**: Provides a clean interface for database access\n2. **Extensibility**: Makes it easy to add new providers\n3. **Consistency**: Ensures consistent access to different data sources\n4. **Discoverability**: Makes available providers easy to discover and use\n\n## Monorepo Architecture Integration\n\n",
        "range": {

        "originalContents": "\n\n    def setup_agents(self):\n        # Web Research Agent\n        self.web_researcher = Assistant(\n            name=\"Web Researcher\",\n            role=\"Research web content and synthesize information\",\n            tools=[DuckDuckGo(), FirecrawlTools()],\n            llm=OpenAIChat(model=\"gpt-4\", temperature=0.7)\n        )\n\n        # Document Analysis Agent\n        self.doc_analyst = Assistant(\n            name=\"Document Analyst\",\n            role=\"Analyze documents and extract key information\",\n            knowledge=self.combined_kb,\n            llm=OpenAIChat(model=\"gpt-4\", temperature=0.5)\n        )\n\n        # Research Team\n        self.research_team = Assistant(\n            name=\"Research Team\",\n            team=[self.web_researcher, self.doc_analyst],\n            llm=OpenAIChat(model=\"gpt-4\", temperature=0.7)\n        )\n\n    def setup_rag_config(self, openai_key: str, anthropic_key: str, cohere_key: str, db_url: str):\n        self.rag_config = RAGLiteConfig(\n            db_url=db_url,\n            llm=\"claude-3-opus-20240229\",\n            embedder=\"text-embedding-3-large\",\n            embedder_normalize=True,\n            chunk_max_size=2000,\n            embedder_sentence_window_size=2\n        )\n\n    async def process_query(self, query: str, user_id: str) -\u003e Dict:\n        # Get relevant memories\n        memories = self.memory.search(query, user_id=user_id, limit=3)\n        memory_context = \" \".join(mem['text'] for mem in memories)\n\n        # Perform RAG search\n        chunks = hybrid_search(query, num_results=5, config=self.rag_config)\n\n        # Research team analysis\n\n        team_response = await self.research_team.arun(research_prompt)\n\n        # Save to memory\n        self.memory.add(\n            text=f\"Research Query: {query}\\nFindings: {team_response}\",\n            user_id=user_id\n        )\n\n        return {\n            \"response\": team_response,\n            \"sources\": chunks,\n            \"memories\": memories\n        }",

        "contents": "# Disclosure RAG System\n\nThis is the Disclosure RAG (Retrieval-Augmented Generation) system, a specialized toolkit for UFO/UAP research and analysis.\n\n## Features\n\n- **Research Agent Framework**: Specialized AI agents for different research tasks\n- **Content Analysis**: Tools for analyzing UFO/UAP-related documents\n- **Knowledge Graph**: Entity extraction and relationship mapping\n- **Enhanced CLI Interface**: Beautiful terminal interface using Charm CLI tools\n  - Interactive prompts with &#96;gum&#96;\n  - Form-based input with &#96;huh&#96;\n  - Markdown rendering with &#96;glow&#96; and &#96;glamour&#96;\n  - Styled terminal output with &#96;bubbletea&#96; and &#96;lipgloss&#96;\n- **Chat Interfaces**: Multiple interfaces for interacting with the Disclosure Assistant\n  - Local chat with knowledge base access\n  - Agno Playground integration\n  - File upload and analysis capabilities\n\n## Recent Additions\n\nThe following components have been migrated from the disclosure-rag-recovered system:\n\n- **Chat Interfaces**: \n  - &#96;disclosure_chat.py&#96;: Local chat interface with knowledge base browsing\n  - &#96;agno_disclosure_chat.py&#96;: Agno Playground chat interface\n  - &#96;agno_disclosure_chat_with_files.py&#96;: Extended Agno interface with file upload support\n- **Automation**: &#96;main.sh&#96; script for common operations\n- **Documentation**: Detailed usage guides in the &#96;docs/&#96; directory\n- **NER Tools**: Enhanced named entity recognition and Xata integration\n\n## Directory Structure\n\n- &#96;agents/&#96;: Specialized AI research agents\n- &#96;analysis/&#96;: Content analysis tools\n- &#96;docs/&#96;: Documentation and research methodologies\n- &#96;ingestion/&#96;: Data ingestion pipelines\n- &#96;lib/&#96;: Shared libraries and utilities\n- &#96;processing/&#96;: Document processing modules\n- &#96;research/&#96;: Research prompts and workflows\n\n## Usage\n\n### Enhanced CLI Interface\n\nThe new interactive CLI provides a beautiful terminal experience:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;bash\n# Interactive CLI with Charm tools\npython cli.py\n# or\ndisclosure-cli\n\n# Try the demo first\npython charm_demo.py\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### Chat Interfaces\n\n",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "# 47-Add-Disclosure-Chat-Modules\n\n**Status:** ⏳ pending\n\n## Title\nAdd Disclosure Chat Modules (&#96;disclosure_chat.py&#96;, &#96;agno_disclosure_chat.py&#96;, &#96;agno_disclosure_chat_with_files.py&#96;)\n\n## Description\nMigrate the three chat/assistant modules from &#96;disclosure-rag-recovered&#96; to &#96;disclosure-rag&#96;. These modules provide chat and assistant functionality not present in the current codebase.\n\n## Acceptance Criteria\n- All three files are present in the appropriate directory (root or &#96;agents/&#96;)\n- Imports and dependencies are updated for the current project structure\n- Modules are discoverable and importable\n- Integration points with existing agents or chat orchestration are documented\n- Basic tests or usage examples are provided\n\n## Implementation Notes\n- For each chat module file:\n  - Copy file to &#96;apps/disclosure-rag/&#96; (or appropriate subdir, e.g., &#96;agents/&#96; if more logical)\n  - Review imports and dependencies; update paths if needed\n  - Integrate with existing agent or chat orchestration if present\n  - Add to &#96;__init__.py&#96; if required for module discovery\n  - Write/adjust tests for new chat modules\n- Review for any hardcoded paths or legacy dependencies\n- Reference: [disclosure_chat.py], [agno_disclosure_chat.py], [agno_disclosure_chat_with_files.py] in recovered\n\n## Effort Estimate\n2-3 points (moderate complexity)\n\n## Testing Guidelines\n- Unit test chat module initialization and basic chat flow\n- Manual test integration with any agent orchestration\n- Run tests after migration to verify integration\n- Update requirements.txt if new dependencies are introduced\n- Document all changes in the migration epic and overview\n\n## References\n- [apps/disclosure-rag/DisclosureRagRecovered_Migration.md]\n- [tickets/DisclosureRagRecovered_Migration_PSEUDOCODE.md] ",

        "contents": "from typing import Optional, Dict, Any\nfrom disclosure_rag.agents.disclosure_assistant import DisclosureAssistant\nfrom disclosure_rag.utils.logger import logger\nimport time\nimport json\nfrom rich.console import Console\nimport os\nfrom openai import OpenAI\n\nconsole = Console()\n\nclass DisclosureAssistant:\n    \"\"\"\n    A modular class for interacting with an OpenAI Assistant specialized in disclosure analysis.\n    Handles thread creation, message management, and assistant interaction.\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, assistant_id: Optional[str] = None, api_key: Optional[str] = None, vector_store_id: Optional[str] = None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize the DisclosureAssistant.\n        \n        Args:\n            assistant_id: The ID of an existing assistant to use. If None, will try to get from env vars.\n            api_key: OpenAI API key. If None, will try to get from env vars.\n            vector_store_id: Optional vector store ID to use. If None, will try to get from env vars.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get(\"OPENAI_API_KEY\")\n        self.client = OpenAI(api_key=self.api_key)\n        \n        # Get assistant ID from parameters or environment variables\n        self.assistant_id = assistant_id or os.environ.get(\"DISCLOSURE_ASSISTANT_ID\")\n        \n        # Get default vector store ID from parameters or environment variables\n        self.vector_store_id = vector_store_id or os.environ.get(\"OPENAI_VECTOR_STORE_ID\")\n        if self.vector_store_id:\n            logger.info(f\"Using vector store ID: {self.vector_store_id}\")\n        \n        if not self.assistant_id:\n            console.print(\"[yellow]Warning: No assistant ID provided and DISCLOSURE_ASSISTANT_ID environment variable not set[/yellow]\")\n            console.print(\"[yellow]Attempting to create a new assistant...[/yellow]\")\n            self.assistant_id = self._create_default_assistant()",

        "originalContents": "from typing import Optional, Dict, Any\nfrom disclosure_rag.agents.disclosure_assistant import DisclosureAssistant\nfrom disclosure_rag.utils.logger import logger\nimport time\nimport json\nfrom rich.console import Console\nimport os\nfrom openai import OpenAI\n\nconsole = Console()\n\nclass DisclosureAssistant:\n    \"\"\"\n    A modular class for interacting with an OpenAI Assistant specialized in disclosure analysis.\n    Handles thread creation, message management, and assistant interaction.\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, assistant_id: Optional[str] = None, api_key: Optional[str] = None, vector_store_id: Optional[str] = None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize the DisclosureAssistant.\n        \n        Args:\n            assistant_id: The ID of an existing assistant to use. If None, will try to get from env vars.\n            api_key: OpenAI API key. If None, will try to get from env vars.\n            vector_store_id: Optional vector store ID to use. If None, will try to get from env vars.\n        \"\"\"\n        self.api_key = api_key or os.environ.get(\"OPENAI_API_KEY\")\n        self.client = OpenAI(api_key=self.api_key)\n        \n        # Get assistant ID from parameters or environment variables\n        self.assistant_id = assistant_id or os.environ.get(\"DISCLOSURE_ASSISTANT_ID\")\n        \n        # Get default vector store ID from parameters or environment variables\n        self.vector_store_id = vector_store_id or os.environ.get(\"OPENAI_VECTOR_STORE_ID\")\n        if self.vector_store_id:\n            logger.info(f\"Using vector store ID: {self.vector_store_id}\")\n        \n        if not self.assistant_id:\n            console.print(\"[yellow]Warning: No assistant ID provided and DISCLOSURE_ASSISTANT_ID environment variable not set[/yellow]\")\n            console.print(\"[yellow]Attempting to create a new assistant...[/yellow]\")\n            self.assistant_id = self._create_default_assistant()",

        "contents": "\n            \n            if run.status == \"completed\":\n                # Retrieve messages\n                messages = self.openai_client.beta.threads.messages.list(\n                    thread_id=thread.id,\n                    order=\"asc\"  # Chronological order\n                )\n                \n                # Extract assistant's messages after our query\n                assistant_responses = []\n                user_message_seen = False\n                \n                for msg in messages.data:\n                    # Mark when we've seen the user's query\n                    if msg.role == \"user\" and user_message_seen == False:\n                        user_message_seen = True\n                        continue\n                    \n                    # Collect assistant's responses that came after user's query\n                    if user_message_seen and msg.role == \"assistant\":\n                        for content_item in msg.content:\n                            if content_item.type == \"text\":\n                                assistant_responses.append(content_item.text.value)\n                \n                # Join all responses\n                return \"\\n\".join(assistant_responses)\n            else:\n                error_msg = f\"Assistant run failed with status: {run.status}\"\n                if hasattr(run, \"last_error\") and run.last_error:\n                    error_msg += f\" - {run.last_error.message}\"\n                logger.error(error_msg)\n                return f\"Analysis failed: {error_msg}\"\n                \n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.error(f\"Error in assistant analysis: {e}\")\n            return f\"Error: {str(e)}\"",

        "originalContents": "\n            \n            if run.status == \"completed\":\n                # Retrieve messages\n                messages = self.openai_client.beta.threads.messages.list(\n                    thread_id=thread.id,\n                    order=\"asc\"  # Chronological order\n                )\n                \n                # Extract assistant's messages after our query\n                assistant_responses = []\n                user_message_seen = False\n                \n                for msg in messages.data:\n                    # Mark when we've seen the user's query\n                    if msg.role == \"user\" and user_message_seen == False:\n                        user_message_seen = True\n                        continue\n                    \n                    # Collect assistant's responses that came after user's query\n                    if user_message_seen and msg.role == \"assistant\":\n                        for content_item in msg.content:\n                            if content_item.type == \"text\":\n                                assistant_responses.append(content_item.text.value)\n                \n                # Join all responses\n                return \"\\n\".join(assistant_responses)\n            else:\n                error_msg = f\"Assistant run failed with status: {run.status}\"\n                if hasattr(run, \"last_error\") and run.last_error:\n                    error_msg += f\" - {run.last_error.message}\"\n                logger.error(error_msg)\n                return f\"Analysis failed: {error_msg}\"\n                \n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.error(f\"Error in assistant analysis: {e}\")\n            return f\"Error: {str(e)}\"",

        "contents": "import json\nimport logging\nimport os\nfrom typing import Dict, Any, Optional, List, Union\nimport time\n\nfrom agno.agent import Agent\nfrom agno.models.anthropic import AnthropicChat\nfrom agno.models.openai import OpenAIChat\nfrom agno.storage.sqlite import SqliteStorage\nfrom openai import OpenAI\n\n# Import research prompt \nfrom research.research_prompt import research_prompt\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\nlogging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)\n\nclass ContentAnalysisAgent:\n    \"\"\"\n    Agent for analyzing content using structured research methodology.\n    Supports multiple LLM providers for comprehensive analysis.\n    \"\"\"\n    \n    def __init__(self, storage_path=\"tmp/content_analysis.db\", vector_store_id=None):\n        \"\"\"\n        Initialize the ContentAnalysisAgent with multiple LLM providers.\n        \n        Args:\n            storage_path: Path to SQLite storage for conversation history\n            vector_store_id: Optional ID of vector store for file search\n        \"\"\"\n        self.claude_model = AnthropicChat(id=\"claude-3-5-sonnet\")\n        self.openai_model = OpenAIChat(id=\"gpt-4o\")\n        self.storage_path = storage_path\n        self.vector_store_id = vector_store_id\n        \n        # Initialize OpenAI client for Assistants API\n        self.openai_client = OpenAI(api_key=os.environ.get(\"OPENAI_API_KEY\"))\n        \n        # Get Assistant ID from environment variable or create a new assistant\n        self.assistant_id = os.environ.get(\"DISCLOSURE_ASSISTANT_ID\")\n        if not self.assistant_id:\n            logger.warning(\"DISCLOSURE_ASSISTANT_ID not found. Creating a new assistant.\")\n            self.assistant_id = self._create_assistant()\n        \n        # Initialize traditional agents\n        self.claude_agent = self._create_claude_agent()\n        self.openai_agent = self._create_openai_agent()",

        "originalContents": "\n        \n        elif workflow_type == \"standard\":\n            # Run entity recognition\n            entity_payload = {\n                \"summary\": \"Identify entities in content\",\n                \"details\": {\"content\": content}\n            }\n            entity_id = await self.submit(\"entity_recognition\", entity_payload, [\"RN\"], \"MEDIUM\")\n            rn_agent = self.agents[\"RN\"]\n            entity_prompt = f\"Analyze the following content for named entities. Provide a structured list of all entities found, categorized by type.\\n\\n{content}\"\n            entity_response = await rn_agent.generate_response(entity_prompt)\n            results[\"entities\"] = entity_response\n            \n            # Run topic classification\n            topic_payload = {\n                \"summary\": \"Classify topics in content\",\n                \"details\": {\"content\": content}\n            }\n            topic_id = await self.submit(\"topic_classification\", topic_payload, [\"TD\"], \"MEDIUM\")\n            td_agent = self.agents[\"TD\"]\n            topic_prompt = f\"Classify the main topics in the following content. Organize by primary and secondary topics with confidence levels.\\n\\n{content}\"\n            topic_response = await td_agent.generate_response(topic_prompt)\n            results[\"topics\"] = topic_response\n            \n            # Run relationship analysis\n            relation_payload = {\n                \"summary\": \"Analyze relationships in content\",\n                \"details\": {\n                    \"entities\": entity_response,\n                    \"topics\": topic_response,\n                    \"content\": content\n                }\n            }\n            relation_id = await self.submit(\"relationship_analysis\", relation_payload, [\"OR\"], \"MEDIUM\")\n            or_agent = self.agents[\"OR\"]",

        "contents": "import json\nimport logging\nimport os\nfrom typing import Any, Dict\n\n# Import the ContentAnalysisEngine and NER prompt.\nfrom agentic_rag.disclosure_data_ingestion.content_analysis import \\\n    ContentAnalysisEngine\nfrom agentic_rag.research.ner_prompt import ner_prompt\n# Import the xata search function from xata_search.py.\nfrom agentic_rag.xata_search import search_record_for_analysis\n\nlogger = logging.getLogger(__name__)\nlogging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)\n\ndef get_structured_entities(analysis_text: str) -\u003e Dict[str, Any]:\n    \"\"\"\n    Uses the AI agent (configured via ContentAnalysisEngine) and the NER prompt to return\n    a structured JSON payload containing recognized entities. Expected keys are:\n      - topics\n      - personnel\n      - events\n      - organizations\n\n    Returns an empty dict if extraction fails.\n    \"\"\"\n    engine = ContentAnalysisEngine()\n    try:\n        # Send the transcript analysis along with the ner_prompt.\n        # This call uses the Anthropic client in ContentAnalysisEngine.\n        message = engine.anthropic_client.messages.create(\n            model=\"claude-3-5-sonnet-20241022\",\n            max_tokens=4000,\n            system=ner_prompt,\n            messages=[\n                {\n                    \"role\": \"user\",\n                    \"content\": analysis_text\n                }\n            ]\n        )\n        # Expecting the agent to return a JSON string.\n        structured_json = message.content[0].text\n        logger.info(\"Raw structured payload received from AI agent:\")\n        logger.info(structured_json)\n        structured_payload = json.loads(structured_json)\n        return structured_payload\n    except Exception as e:\n        logger.error(f\"Error extracting structured entities: {e}\")\n        return {}",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "# Disclosure Assistant Chat Interface\n\nThis implementation provides a local chat interface for interacting with the Disclosure Assistant using Agno Playground, with direct access to the local knowledge base.\n\n## Features\n\n- Interactive chat interface via Agno Playground\n- Direct access to Disclosure Assistant's analysis capabilities\n- Support for analyzing text content and uploaded files\n- Cross-reference analysis tool for enhanced insights\n- Browse and read local knowledge base files\n\n## Setup\n\n1. Ensure you have the required dependencies:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n   pip install -r requirements.txt\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Set up your environment variables:\n   - &#96;OPENAI_API_KEY&#96;: Your OpenAI API key\n   - &#96;OPENAI_ASSISTANT_ID&#96;: ID of your disclosure assistant (optional)\n   - &#96;OPENAI_VECTOR_STORE_ID&#96;: ID of your vector store for knowledge base (optional)\n\n3. Run the chat interface:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n   python disclosure_chat.py\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Available Tools\n\nThe chat interface exposes the following tools:\n\n### 1. Content Analysis\n\nAnalyze any text content using the Disclosure Assistant:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nanalyze_content(content: str, custom_instructions: Optional[str])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. Cross-Reference Analysis\n\nEnhance an existing analysis with data from the knowledge base:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ncross_reference_analysis(original_analysis: str, custom_instructions: Optional[str])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Browse Knowledge Base Files\n\nList files in a specific directory of the knowledge base:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nlist_knowledge_base_files(directory: str, pattern: Optional[str])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nKey directories include:\n- &#96;transcripts&#96; - UFO/UAP testimonies and interviews\n- &#96;case_files&#96; - Detailed information on specific UFO/UAP cases\n- &#96;vector-store-files&#96; - Processed documents for vector search\n\n### 4. Read Knowledge Base Files\n\nRead the content of specific knowledge base files:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nread_knowledge_base_file(file_path: str)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Example Workflows\n\n### Analyzing New Content\n\n1.         "originalContents": "# Disclosure Assistant Chat Interface\n\nThis implementation provides a local chat interface for interacting with the Disclosure Assistant using Agno Playground, with direct access to the local knowledge base.\n\n## Features\n\n- Interactive chat interface via Agno Playground\n- Direct access to Disclosure Assistant's analysis capabilities\n- Support for analyzing text content and uploaded files\n- Cross-reference analysis tool for enhanced insights\n- Browse and read local knowledge base files\n\n## Setup\n\n1. Ensure you have the required dependencies:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n   pip install -r requirements.txt\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n2. Set up your environment variables:\n   - &#96;OPENAI_API_KEY&#96;: Your OpenAI API key\n   - &#96;OPENAI_ASSISTANT_ID&#96;: ID of your disclosure assistant (optional)\n   - &#96;OPENAI_VECTOR_STORE_ID&#96;: ID of your vector store for knowledge base (optional)\n\n3. Run the chat interface:\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n   python disclosure_chat.py\n   &#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Available Tools\n\nThe chat interface exposes the following tools:\n\n### 1. Content Analysis\n\nAnalyze any text content using the Disclosure Assistant:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nanalyze_content(content: str, custom_instructions: Optional[str])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 2. Cross-Reference Analysis\n\nEnhance an existing analysis with data from the knowledge base:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\ncross_reference_analysis(original_analysis: str, custom_instructions: Optional[str])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n### 3. Browse Knowledge Base Files\n\nList files in a specific directory of the knowledge base:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nlist_knowledge_base_files(directory: str, pattern: Optional[str])\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\nKey directories include:\n- &#96;transcripts&#96; - UFO/UAP testimonies and interviews\n- &#96;case_files&#96; - Detailed information on specific UFO/UAP cases\n- &#96;vector-store-files&#96; - Processed documents for vector search\n\n### 4. Read Knowledge Base Files\n\nRead the content of specific knowledge base files:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nread_knowledge_base_file(file_path: str)\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n## Example Workflows\n\n### Analyzing New Content\n\n1.         "contents": "\n        try:\n            store_id = vector_store_id or self.vector_store_id\n            \n            # Create a new vector store if needed\n            if not store_id:\n                logger.info(\"Creating new vector store\")\n                store = self.openai_client.beta.vector_stores.create(\n                    name=\"disclosure-research-kb\"\n                )\n                store_id = store.id\n                self.vector_store_id = store_id\n            \n            # Upload file to OpenAI\n            logger.info(f\"Uploading file: {file_path}\")\n            with open(file_path, \"rb\") as f:\n                file = self.openai_client.files.create(\n                    file=f,\n                    purpose=\"assistants\"\n                )\n            \n            # Add file to vector store\n            logger.info(f\"Adding file to vector store: {store_id}\")\n            file_upload = self.openai_client.beta.vector_stores.files.create_and_poll(\n                vector_store_id=store_id,\n                file_id=file.id\n            )\n            \n            return {\n                \"status\": \"success\",\n                \"vector_store_id\": store_id,\n                \"file_id\": file.id,\n                \"details\": file_upload\n            }\n            \n        except Exception as e:\n            logger.error(f\"Error uploading file to vector store: {e}\")\n            return {\n                \"status\": \"error\",\n                \"error\": str(e)\n            }",

        "contents": "# Disclosure RAG - Agent System\n\n## Agent Organization\n\nAgents are organized into three primary categories:\n\n### 1. Extraction Agents \n*Located in &#96;agents/extraction/&#96;*\n\n- Convert raw inputs (text, files, media) into structured artifacts \n- Focus on entity extraction, not reasoning\n- Examples: &#96;EntityExtractionAgent&#96;\n\n### 2. Analysis Agents\n*Located in &#96;agents/analysis/&#96;*\n\n- Perform reasoning, correlation, verification, and visualization\n- Answer questions, build graphs, search external sources\n- Examples: &#96;ContentAnalysisAgent&#96;, &#96;KnowledgeGraphAssistant&#96;, &#96;LocalRAGAssistant&#96;, &#96;OracleAssistant&#96;, &#96;DisclosureAssistant&#96;\n\n### 3. Orchestration\n*Located in &#96;agents/orchestration/&#96;*\n\n- Coordinate multiple agents to accomplish complex tasks\n- Manage workflows and pipelines\n- Examples: &#96;ContentAnalysisEngine&#96;, &#96;ResearchCrew&#96;\n\n## Research Crew Refactoring\n\nThe &#96;research_crew.py&#96; file defines specialized agents (HA, CE, GV, etc.) inline. We are progressively extracting these into individual modules in the &#96;orchestration/research_crew/specialized/&#96; directory.\n\nProgress:\n- [x] Created directory structure\n- [x] Created &#96;historical_timeline_agent.py&#96; as a template\n- [ ] Extract other agent definitions\n- [ ] Update &#96;crew.py&#96; to use the extracted modules\n\n## Documentation\n\nComprehensive documentation for all agents is available in:\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/ExtractionAgents.md&#96;\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/AnalysisAgents.md&#96;\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/ResearchCrew.md&#96;",

        "contents": "# Disclosure RAG – Prompt Inventory\n\nThis document provides a comprehensive inventory of **every prompt, prompt file, and prompt configuration** found in the &#96;apps/&#96;, &#96;app/&#96;, &#96;disclosure-rag/&#96;, and &#96;docs/&#96; directories. It includes all explicit prompt strings, prompt files, prompt templates, and configuration mappings for agent prompts.\n\n---\n\n## 1. Prompt Files \u0026 Prompt Definitions\n\n### A. Python Code: Prompt Strings \u0026 Mappings\n\n#### &#96;apps/disclosure-rag/agents/prompts.py&#96;\n- **Purpose:** Centralized mapping of all specialized agent prompts.\n- **Key Variable:** &#96;AGENT_PROMPTS&#96; (dict mapping agent type to prompt string)\n- **Example:**\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;python\n  AGENT_PROMPTS = {\n      \"historical\": \"\"\"You are an expert historical analyst specializing in UFO/UAP events chronology...\"\"\",\n      \"claims_evidence\": \"\"\"You are an expert evidence analyst specializing in UAP phenomena documentation...\"\"\",\n      ...\n  }\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;\n- **Also contains:** &#96;AGENT_CONFIG&#96; (agent tag, name, model_id, agent_type)\n\n---\n\n#### &#96;apps/disclosure-rag/agents/&#96; (Individual Agent Files)\n- **Each agent file** (e.g., &#96;claims_evidence_agent.py&#96;, &#96;dataviz_agent.py&#96;, etc.) either:\n  - Imports its prompt from &#96;AGENT_PROMPTS&#96; (above), or\n  - Defines an inline prompt string (sometimes as a fallback or for legacy reasons).\n\n**Examples:**\n- &#96;claims_evidence_agent.py&#96;:\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;python\n  prompt = AGENT_PROMPTS.get(\"claims_evidence\", \"You are a UAP/UFO evidence analysis assistant.\")\n  &#96;&#96;&#96;\n- &#96;geospatial_agent.py&#96;, &#96;network_agent.py&#96;, &#96;historical_agent.py&#96;, etc.:\n  - Each defines a multi-line string prompt (e.g., &#96;GEOSPATIAL_PROMPT&#96;, &#96;HISTORICAL_PROMPT&#96;, &#96;NETWORK_PROMPT&#96;).\n\n---\n\n#### &#96;apps/disclosure-rag/agents/research_crew.py&#96;\n- **Contains:** Large inline dictionaries for &#96;AGENT_PROMPTS&#96; and &#96;AGENT_CONFIG&#96; (mirrors &#96;prompts.py&#96;).\n- **Purpose:** Used to instantiate all agents in the research crew with their respective prompts.\n\n---\n\n#### &#96;apps/disclosure-rag/agents/content_analysis_agent.py&#96;\n",

        "contents": "\n    \n    def _run_assistant_analysis(self, content: str) -\u003e str:\n        \"\"\"\n        Run analysis using OpenAI Assistant API with proper handling of threads and runs.\n        \n        Args:\n            content: The text content to analyze\n            \n        Returns:\n            Analysis from the assistant\n        \"\"\"\n        try:\n            logger.info(\"Starting OpenAI Assistant analysis\")\n            \n            # Create a new thread\n            thread = self.openai_client.beta.threads.create()\n            \n            # Add content as a message to the thread\n            self.openai_client.beta.threads.messages.create(\n                thread_id=thread.id,\n                role=\"user\",\n                content=f\"Analyze the following content according to our research methodology:\\n\\n{content}\"\n            )\n            \n            # Create run parameters with custom instructions\n            run_params = {\n                \"thread_id\": thread.id,\n                \"assistant_id\": self.assistant_id,\n                \"instructions\": \"Organize your analysis into clear sections for topics, personnel, events, and organizations. Provide detailed research findings using all available tools and evidence.\"\n            }\n            \n            # Add vector store if available\n            if self.vector_store_id:\n                run_params[\"tool_resources\"] = {\n                    \"file_search\": {\"vector_store_ids\": [self.vector_store_id]}\n                }\n            \n            # Execute the run and wait for completion\n            run = self.openai_client.beta.threads.runs.create(**run_params)\n            \n            # Poll for completion\n            run = self._wait_on_run(thread.id, run.id)",

        "contents": "go install github.com/charmbracelet/glamour@latest\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Note:** The CLI will work without Charm tools but with reduced functionality.\n\n## Configuration\n\nCreate a &#96;.env&#96; file with the following variables:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nOPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key\nANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_api_key\nOPENAI_ASSISTANT_ID=your_assistant_id\nOPENAI_VECTOR_STORE_ID=your_vector_store_id\nKNOWLEDGE_BASE_PATH=./knowledge\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n\n# Disclosure RAG - Agent System\n\n## Agent Organization\n\nAgents are organized into three primary categories:\n\n### 1. Extraction Agents \n*Located in &#96;agents/extraction/&#96;*\n\n- Convert raw inputs (text, files, media) into structured artifacts \n- Focus on entity extraction, not reasoning\n- Examples: &#96;EntityExtractionAgent&#96;\n\n### 2. Analysis Agents\n*Located in &#96;agents/analysis/&#96;*\n\n- Perform reasoning, correlation, verification, and visualization\n- Answer questions, build graphs, search external sources\n- Examples: &#96;ContentAnalysisAgent&#96;, &#96;KnowledgeGraphAssistant&#96;, &#96;LocalRAGAssistant&#96;, &#96;OracleAssistant&#96;, &#96;DisclosureAssistant&#96;\n\n### 3. Orchestration\n*Located in &#96;agents/orchestration/&#96;*\n\n- Coordinate multiple agents to accomplish complex tasks\n- Manage workflows and pipelines\n- Examples: &#96;ContentAnalysisEngine&#96;, &#96;ResearchCrew&#96;\n\n## Research Crew Refactoring\n\nThe &#96;research_crew.py&#96; file defines specialized agents (HA, CE, GV, etc.) inline. We are progressively extracting these into individual modules in the &#96;orchestration/research_crew/specialized/&#96; directory.\n\nProgress:\n- [x] Created directory structure\n- [x] Created &#96;historical_timeline_agent.py&#96; as a template\n- [ ] Extract other agent definitions\n- [ ] Update &#96;crew.py&#96; to use the extracted modules\n\n## Documentation\n\nComprehensive documentation for all agents is available in:\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/ExtractionAgents.md&#96;\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/AnalysisAgents.md&#96;\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/ResearchCrew.md&#96;\n",

        "originalContents": "go install github.com/charmbracelet/glamour@latest\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n**Note:** The CLI will work without Charm tools but with reduced functionality.\n\n## Configuration\n\nCreate a &#96;.env&#96; file with the following variables:\n\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\nOPENAI_API_KEY=your_api_key\nANTHROPIC_API_KEY=your_api_key\nOPENAI_ASSISTANT_ID=your_assistant_id\nOPENAI_VECTOR_STORE_ID=your_vector_store_id\nKNOWLEDGE_BASE_PATH=./knowledge\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\n\n\n\n# Disclosure RAG - Agent System\n\n## Agent Organization\n\nAgents are organized into three primary categories:\n\n### 1. Extraction Agents \n*Located in &#96;agents/extraction/&#96;*\n\n- Convert raw inputs (text, files, media) into structured artifacts \n- Focus on entity extraction, not reasoning\n- Examples: &#96;EntityExtractionAgent&#96;\n\n### 2. Analysis Agents\n*Located in &#96;agents/analysis/&#96;*\n\n- Perform reasoning, correlation, verification, and visualization\n- Answer questions, build graphs, search external sources\n- Examples: &#96;ContentAnalysisAgent&#96;, &#96;KnowledgeGraphAssistant&#96;, &#96;LocalRAGAssistant&#96;, &#96;OracleAssistant&#96;, &#96;DisclosureAssistant&#96;\n\n### 3. Orchestration\n*Located in &#96;agents/orchestration/&#96;*\n\n- Coordinate multiple agents to accomplish complex tasks\n- Manage workflows and pipelines\n- Examples: &#96;ContentAnalysisEngine&#96;, &#96;ResearchCrew&#96;\n\n## Research Crew Refactoring\n\nThe &#96;research_crew.py&#96; file defines specialized agents (HA, CE, GV, etc.) inline. We are progressively extracting these into individual modules in the &#96;orchestration/research_crew/specialized/&#96; directory.\n\nProgress:\n- [x] Created directory structure\n- [x] Created &#96;historical_timeline_agent.py&#96; as a template\n- [ ] Extract other agent definitions\n- [ ] Update &#96;crew.py&#96; to use the extracted modules\n\n## Documentation\n\nComprehensive documentation for all agents is available in:\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/ExtractionAgents.md&#96;\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/AnalysisAgents.md&#96;\n- &#96;packages/docs/architecture/ResearchCrew.md&#96;\n",

        "contents": "- **exportCompositeData**: Exports data in various formats (JSON, Markdown, CSV)\n\n#### UI Components\n\n- **Tab Navigation**: Allows switching between pipeline views\n- **Composite View**: Displays aggregated data and insights\n- **Document Pipeline**: Processes text documents\n- **Web Pipeline**: Analyzes web resources\n- **Agent Pipeline**: Executes AI agent workflows\n\n### Features\n\n- **Cross-pipeline Analysis**: Identifies common themes and patterns across all data sources\n- **Detailed Insights**: Generates comprehensive analysis of combined data\n- **Data Export**: Downloads composite data in multiple formats\n- **AI Context Integration**: Registers composite data with AI assistants\n\n### Extensibility\n\n- To add a new pipeline:\n  1.       "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "\n## Feature Roadmap\n\n### **1. Major Historical UFO Event Chronology**\n\n**a. Beautiful 3D Visuals of All UFO Sightings by Location**\n\n- **Interactive World Map**: Implement a dynamic, zoomable 3D globe where users can explore UFO sightings globally.\n- **Time Slider**: Allow users to navigate through time to see how sightings have evolved over decades.\n- **Heatmaps**: Display density of sightings in specific regions or time periods.\n- **Augmented Reality (AR) Integration**: Enable users to visualize historical sightings in their current location using AR.\n\n**b. Detailed Event Pages**\n\n- **Comprehensive Descriptions**: Provide in-depth information about each event, including eyewitness accounts, official reports, and media coverage.\n- **Multimedia Integration**: Incorporate photos, videos, audio recordings, and interactive media related to each event.\n- **Geospatial Data**: Show precise locations with satellite imagery and maps.\n- **User Annotations**: Allow users to add comments or additional information to each event.\n\n### **2. Status Reporting on Claims, Hearings, News Items, and Events**\n\n**a. Progress Reporting**\n\n- **Dashboard Overview**: Present a real-time dashboard highlighting recent developments, ongoing investigations, and upcoming events.\n- **Timeline Tracking**: Visual timelines showing the progression of key claims and hearings.\n- **Notification System**: Enable users to subscribe to updates on specific topics or events.\n\n**b. Categorization and Filtering**\n\n- **Filter by Date, Region, or Topic**: Allow users to sort and view status reports based on their interests.\n- **Priority Indicators**: Highlight high-impact or high-interest items for quick access.\n\n### **3. Topic Tracker**\n\n**a. Dynamic Topic Mapping**\n\n- **Interconnected Topics**: Visualize how different topics relate to each other using network graphs.\n- **Trending Topics**: Highlight emerging topics and their growth over time.\n",

        "contents": "\n\nexport function DocumentStatus({\n  document: initialDocument,\n  tasks: initialTasks,\n  onUpdate,\n  className,\n}: DocumentStatusProps) {\n  const [document, setDocument] = useState(initialDocument)\n  const [tasks, setTasks] = useState(initialTasks)\n  const [error, setError] = useState\u003cstring | null\u003e(null)\n\n  useEffect(() =\u003e {\n    let timeoutId: NodeJS.Timeout\n    const POLL_INTERVAL = 5000 // 5 seconds\n\n    const pollStatus = async () =\u003e {\n      try {\n        const result = await getDocumentStatus(document.id)\n\n        if (!result.success) {\n          throw new Error(result.error)\n        }\n\n        setDocument(result.document)\n        setTasks(result.tasks)\n        onUpdate?.(result.document, result.tasks)\n\n        // Continue polling if document is still processing\n        if (result.document.status === 'processing') {\n          timeoutId = setTimeout(pollStatus, POLL_INTERVAL)\n        }\n      } catch (err) {\n        setError(err instanceof Error ? err.message : 'Failed to fetch status')\n        console.error('Error polling status:', err)\n      }\n    }\n\n    // Only start polling if the document is in processing state\n    if (document.status === 'processing') {\n      timeoutId = setTimeout(pollStatus, POLL_INTERVAL)\n    }\n\n    return () =\u003e {\n      if (timeoutId) clearTimeout(timeoutId)\n    }\n  }, [document.id, document.status, onUpdate])\n\n  const getDocumentProgress = () =\u003e {\n    if (tasks.length === 0) return 0\n    const completedTasks = tasks.filter((task) =\u003e task.status === 'processed').length\n    return Math.round((completedTasks / tasks.length) * 100)\n  }\n\n  const getLatestTask = () =\u003e {\n    return tasks.sort(\n      (a, b) =\u003e new Date(b.created_at).getTime() - new Date(a.created_at).getTime()\n    )[0]\n  }\n\n  const progress = getDocumentProgress()\n  const latestTask = getLatestTask()\n  const isProcessing = document.status === 'processing'\n  const isError = document.status === 'error' || error",

+ # Ultraterrestrial - Application State Report
+ **Generated:** January 15, 2025 | **Branch:** feat/code-recovery

+ ## Project Overview

+ **Ultraterrestrial** is a UFO/UAP disclosure tracking platform designed as the definitive hub for exploring the "state of disclosure" through data visualization, AI analysis, and collaborative research tools. Currently in active development with substantial progress across multiple domains.

+ - **apps/cli/** - Command-line tools with enhanced Charm UI
+ - **packages/** - Shared libraries (db, ai, knowledge-base, docs, services)
+ 
+ ### Tech Stack
+ - **Frontend:** Next.js 15, React 19, TypeScript, Tailwind, shadcn/ui
+ - **3D Graphics:** Three.js, React Three Fiber, GSAP
+ - **Database:** Xata (primary), Supabase (migration target)
